bounded_leaf.tested_scope: Deterministic role-local synthetic fixtures only. No public sources, repository chronology beyond own current STATE, other-role state, O/downstream semantics, real external effect, scheduler mutation, wait/retry, or second leaf was used.

assumptions: The publication winner is still determined by exact full-record identity before any effect call.
The same logical attempt can reconstruct and reuse the exact stable sink idempotency key attempt_identity/replay_key across restart.
The sink durably deduplicates repeated submissions under that key and treats reuse with a different payload as invalid rather than as a second effect.
Sink idempotency is an existing destination capability and does not require richer-mode execution, a finite monthly/trial/paid quota, paid infrastructure, or manual intervention.

case_matrix.recovery: retry publication-owner CAS EMPTY->CLAIMED, then submit exact stable sink key A1/K1
re-submit A1/K1 to idempotent sink; first accepted submission applies once, then mark local COMPLETED
re-submit A1/K1; sink returns/deduplicates prior logical effect, then local COMPLETED may be written
local completion short-circuits; redundant sink submission with A1/K1 would also deduplicate

redesign_A_sink_native_idempotency.result: Within the synthetic model, a durable sink-native stable idempotency key removes the CLAIMED ambiguity across separate local/sink commit domains: replay may safely re-submit the same logical effect whether the pre-crash call happened or not, so no-duplicate safety and eventual application can both hold.
redesign_A_sink_native_idempotency.limitation: The result is conditional on exact stable-key reconstruction and durable sink semantics. This leaf does not prove a concrete zero-quota sink capability or a collision-safe concurrent attempt_identity/replay_key allocation rule.

redesign_B_atomic_outbox_or_transaction_.model: Couple guard state and final effect publication in one atomic commit domain. A transaction either commits both the effect and completion identity or commits neither.

case_matrix.recovery: observe committed-or-not atomically; retry only if not committed
replay observes committed publication identity and does not publish a second effect
unique publication identity returns existing committed result

redesign_B_atomic_outbox_or_transaction_.outbox_boundary_check: An ordinary outbox that atomically commits only guard+outbox-record, while the actual non-idempotent sink remains a separate later delivery domain, does not by itself solve the original crash window. A crash after external delivery but before durable outbox acknowledgement recreates the same applied-vs-not-applied ambiguity unless the sink deduplicates a stable key or the delivery participates in an atomic transaction with the sink.
redesign_B_atomic_outbox_or_transaction_.result: Atomic coupling restores both safety and liveness when the final effect itself is inside the same atomic commit domain. Outbox-only enqueue is insufficient for an arbitrary separate non-idempotent external effect; it shifts rather than removes the ambiguity.

comparison.separate_commit_domains: Redesign A is sufficient under durable sink idempotency; Redesign B is insufficient if it is merely an outbox feeding a separate non-idempotent sink.
comparison.single_commit_domain: Redesign B is sufficient when the final effect and guard/identity are one atomic commit; Redesign A is not required for correctness in that restricted scope.
comparison.preferred_general_recovery_shape: For separate local and effect destinations, require a destination-level stable idempotency key and reconstruct the exact same key on replay. Use atomic same-domain publication when available; do not treat an outbox alone as exactly-once external delivery.

bounded_leaf.validated_property: The prior safety-vs-liveness impossibility is not inherent once the effect destination contributes either durable same-key deduplication or true same-domain atomic commit. Stable sink idempotency resolves the cross-domain crash ambiguity; true atomic coupling removes the cross-domain boundary. An outbox record without idempotent/transactional delivery does neither.
unresolved_conditions: A concrete zero-quota concurrent rule that allocates or reconstructs attempt_identity/replay_key without collision or accidental key drift remains untested.
No concrete sink was verified to provide durable idempotency semantics with optional monthly/trial/paid quota at zero; this leaf tests mechanism logic only.
No concrete same-domain transaction surface was verified for an arbitrary external non-idempotent effect; outbox enqueue alone is explicitly not counted as sufficient.
